content:
A thought from a fresher lawyer. ⚖️

One thing I’ve noticed while applying for legal jobs is that many companies ask for 2, 3, 5, or even 10 years of experience for roles that are still being offered at fresher-level salaries.

And honestly, I sometimes wonder:

If I already had 5 or 10 years of solid litigation experience, why would I be applying for a ₹20,000–₹30,000 job?

With that much experience in litigation, I would already have built my own practice, client base, and professional standing.

I completely understand that companies need skilled and experienced professionals. But how does a fresher ever become experienced if nobody is willing to give them their first opportunity?

We freshers are not asking for a shortcut.

We are asking for one opportunity to learn, contribute, and prove ourselves.

We may not have 5 years of experience, but we have:
• Legal education
• The willingness to learn
• Research skills
• The ability to adapt
• And most importantly, the hunger to build our careers

If every organisation asks for experience, then where exactly should freshers go to gain that experience?

To all companies and recruiters in the legal sector, I have just one humble request:

Please consider giving freshers a chance.

Someone has to give us the first opportunity.

Because today’s fresher can become tomorrow’s experienced professional, but only if someone is willing to let them start.
